title: After death
caption:
What happens to your body after you die? 💀

It doesn't switch off all at once. About 10 seconds after the heart stops, brain waves start to fade. In a 2023 study, 2 of 4 dying patients showed a sudden surge of brain activity. The body cools about 1 °C an hour, blood settles within about 2 hours, and muscles stiffen for about a day. And in mice and zebrafish, over 1,000 genes changed their activity after death, for up to 4 days.

title: Voice on recordings
caption:
Why Your Voice Sounds So Weird on Recordings 🎙️

When you talk, your voice reaches your inner ear two ways: through the air and through the bones of your skull. Bone carries the low notes best, so you sound deeper in your head. A microphone only hears the air. Try it: plug your ears and hum.

title: Profit vs sales
caption:
Sales up 50%. Profit down by half. How? 📉

Profit = sales − costs, and costs can grow faster than sales. Discounts, ads, delivery and extra staff ate the bakery's margin: from $20 of every $100 kept, to under $7. Watch margins, not just sales.

title: How Many Days Are Left With Your Parents
caption:
How many days do you have left with your parents? If you're 25, they're 55, and you visit twice a year, it may be only about 500 days 💛

Until 18 you saw them almost every day; you've already spent about 93% of your time with them. Every visit home takes 10 of what's left.

500 days. Not years. Days. Go home more often, and call them today. Share this with someone who lives away from home 🏠

title: Glitch 5 - Car sickness
caption:
Why does reading in a car make you sick? 🚗🤢

Your eyes say you're sitting still; your inner ear feels every turn. That mismatch is the leading explanation. The strongest clue: people whose balance organs don't work almost never get motion sick. Fix: look at the horizon.

title: Glitch 6 - Running in dreams
caption:
Why can't you run in your dreams? 🏃‍♀️💤

In dream sleep your brain switches your muscles off, using GABA and glycine, so you don't act out your dreams. In a study of lucid dreamers, walking a set number of steps took about 50% longer in the dream than awake.

title: Clock freezes
caption:
Why the Clock Freezes When You First Look at It ⏱️

Your eyes jump about three times a second, and your brain switches vision off during every jump. When they land, it pastes that first view backwards in time, so the first tick looks longer: about 0.12 s in one experiment.

Rub your eyes and you see stars ✨👁️

title: Spit disgust
caption:
Why Your Own Spit Disgusts You Outside Your Mouth 🤢

You swallow up to a litre and a half of saliva a day without a thought. But psychologist Paul Rozin found almost nobody would eat their favourite soup after spitting in it. Disgust is your body's germ alarm: once something leaves you, it's a stranger.

title: Dark space
caption:
Why Is Space Dark If There Are Trillions of Stars? 🌌

If space went on forever, every line of sight would end on a star and the sky would blaze. It's dark because the universe is about 13.8 billion years old, so far light hasn't reached us, and expansion stretches the rest out of sight. Olbers' paradox.

caption:
Brain freeze isn't your brain freezing 🍦🥶

Cold hits the roof of your mouth, the trigeminal nerve sends the alarm, and your brain feels it in your forehead: referred pain. In a 2002 study, eating ice cream fast gave twice as many people brain freeze. A warm tongue on the roof of your mouth may help.

title: Glitch 3 - Doorway memory
caption:
Why do you forget what you came into a room for? 🚪🧠

Psychologists call it the doorway effect: your brain files life in scenes, and a doorway can start a new one. But science is honest: a 2021 study found the effect in only one of four tests, when people's minds were already busy.
